summary: Elevated chat prelude latency and intermittent 504s after runtime snapshot & model adapter update
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Aurelia Health, enterprise/dedicated) reports a sustained increase in prelude latency (time between request acceptance and first token emission) for short chat completions starting immediately after our runtime snapshot + model adapter update on 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC. Some requests escalate to 504 gateway timeouts when the first-token delay exceeds the proxy timeout.

Impact:
- Increased TTFB for ~70% of short-prompt chat sessions during peak for the customer's dedicated pools in us-east-1.
- ~2% of requests hit 504s during the peak window, causing customer app errors and increased support load.
- Affects production traffic only; staging unaffected.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (cust-dedicated-az1-us-east)
- Runtime snapshot: runtime-snapshot-2026-03-09-a
- Model adapter update: chat-adapter-v2.7 deployed to dedicated pools as part of the snapshot
- Region: us-east-1

Steps to reproduce (observed by Support):
1) Create a short chat prompt (~12 tokens) and request streaming completion via /v1/chat/complete on the customer's API key.
2) Observe request acceptance but delay in streaming start (30–1200 ms increase baseline) before first token emitted.
3) Repeated runs show high variance; longer prompts less impacted.

Observed behavior:
- Median TTFB increased from ~85ms to ~360ms for short prompts. Tail (95th) increased from ~220ms to ~1.4s.
- Some streams never start and result in 504 at the edge.
- No model-quality regressions observed in outputs.

Expected behavior:
- Short prompts should see first token within <150ms median on dedicated pools per SLA.
- Streaming should begin reliably without hitting the proxy timeout.

Logs / telemetry references:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency/chat-prelude?orgId=1&var-pool=cust-dedicated-az1-us-east
- Edge logs: edge-proxy/2026-03-09T03:12:45Z TRACE request-id=abc123 status=accepted backend=runtime-42
- Runtime logs (snippet): 
  [2026-03-09T03:12:45.120Z] runtime-42 INFO accept request req=abc123 kernel=auto select_path=compat
  [2026-03-09T03:12:45.450Z] runtime-42 WARN kv-cache:prefix-miss key=conv-79 eviction=evict-oldest
  [2026-03-09T03:12:46.250Z] runtime-42 ERROR stream-start-delay req=abc123 elapsed_ms=1130 stage=kv-load

Temporary workaround implemented:
- SRE routed Aurelia Health traffic off the new runtime-snapshot-2026-03-09-a to the prior snapshot for the affected dedicated pools at 2026-03-11T01:30Z. This reduced median TTFB back to ~90ms and eliminated observed 504s for the customer.

Next steps / escalation:
- Engineering (serving-runtime) and Scheduler are engaged to triage root cause.
- Prioritized items: reproduce in-house, trace kernel selection & kv-cache behavior for short prompts, audit warmup/coldstart signals introduced in the snapshot, review scheduler affinity changes in PR 112.
- Customer notified and monitoring continues.

Notes: Avoid long-form postmortem in ticket; a separate incident postmortem will be created if root cause is confirmed.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Kernel selection change in snapshot causes short-sequence requests to take a slower execution path (compat/soft-fallback) that triggers an extra KV prefetch stage, increasing TTFB.
Hypothesis B: Scheduler affinity change (PR 112) delayed hot-slot assignment for short jobs causing queueing and head-of-line blocking at the runtime acceptor layer.

Repro steps run in lab: synthetic short prompts against runtime-snapshot-2026-03-09-a with identical request patterns reproduce median TTFB increase. Enabling legacy kernel path removes the regression in lab.
Additional observation: kv-cache eviction occurred more frequently after snapshot; eviction appears correlated with adapter v2.7 prefix hashing change.
Temporary mitigation validated by routing customer traffic to previous snapshot; suggests regression introduced in snapshot rather than customer config.
resolution: Mitigation applied: customer traffic routed back to previous runtime snapshot and observed latency returned to baseline. Engineering teams are coordinating a targeted rollback or patch to runtime-snapshot-2026-03-09-a that disables the new kernel-selection heuristics and restores previous kv-cache prefix behavior for dedicated pools. Permanent fix ETA TBD; follow-up ticket will be created for full postmortem and rollout plan.
workaround: Route affected customer dedicated pools off the problematic snapshot (done). For self-serve customers, recommend pinning to previous snapshot or contacting support to request pool routing until patch is released.
